reference_policy_design: The policy adapter is 'default' and the reference adapter is 'ref'; both begin from the same trained SFT adapter state (outputs/qlora_adapter, loaded once as 'default' with no custom adapter_name). train_dpo.py passes ref_model=None to DPOTrainer; the installed TRL 1.14.0 creates the 'ref' adapter automatically inside its own constructor (reading model.peft_config['default']) and copies every .default. parameter into the matching .ref. parameter, giving a frozen copy of the instruction-tuned state without loading a second full model. PEFT 0.20.0 supports this path. train_dpo.py's verify_reference_setup() runs after DPOTrainer construction and before trainer.train() -- it checks (not assumes) that both adapters exist, 'default' is trainable, 'ref' is fully frozen, and their starting tensors are exact copies, failing loudly otherwise. The installed DPOConfig does not expose model_adapter_name/ref_adapter_name -- an earlier design assumed those existed and manually built two named adapters; that assumption did not hold against the real installed API and has been removed.
max_length_status: APPROVED, and the value actually passed to DPOConfig at runtime. Selected from the real Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizer audit run in Google Colab against the 150-pair controlled DPO dataset (data/dpo_pairs.jsonl) -- see data/dpo_pairs_audit.json. Measured: prompt+chosen max 215 tokens, prompt+rejected max 217 tokens; max_length=256 preserves every one of those sequences with modest headroom.
max_prompt_length_status: AUDIT DOCUMENTATION ONLY -- NOT passed to DPOConfig at runtime. The real tokenizer audit found prompt tokens max=155, so 192 would preserve all 150 prompts with headroom, but the installed TRL 1.14.0 DPOConfig does not expose max_prompt_length as a parameter (verified against the live Colab API). The runtime instead relies on max_length=256 alone, which the same audit showed preserves every prompt+chosen and prompt+rejected sequence (maxima 215 and 217 tokens respectively). Do not pass this value to DPOConfig -- it will raise a TypeError against the installed version.
